metadata.note: The Wilmington and Weldon Railroad -- the line that actually reached Wilmington, NC, extending the Petersburg Railroad's Virginia-North Carolina chain (see petersburg_railroad.geojson) another 161.5 miles south to the coast. Chartered Jan 1834 as the Wilmington and Raleigh Railroad (despite the name, it never reached Raleigh -- built instead via Goldsboro and Rocky Mount to connect with the Petersburg Railroad at Weldon), it was completed Mar 7 1840 and was, at that moment, the longest railroad in the world. Renamed the Wilmington and Weldon in 1855. From 1871 it was marketed alongside sister roads under the 'Atlantic Coast Line' name even while remaining a formally separate company (all under Baltimore investor William T. Walters' control), until the Apr 21 1900 merger that created the actual Atlantic Coast Line Railroad Company -- headquartered in Wilmington itself. That HQ moved to Jacksonville, FL in 1960, and Wilmington's last passenger train left Union Station in 1968; unlike the Petersburg Railroad's corridor, this route lost through passenger service for good (today's Amtrak/CSX Silver Meteor-Palmetto corridor bypasses Wilmington on a more direct alignment). GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search), with two short hand-placed bridges (~7km and ~6km) where Overpass found no connected path even including abandoned ways -- likely genuine gaps in what survives of this corridor today. Traced length 268.7 km / 167.0 mi, close to the sourced 161.5 mi.
